nodes.role: Python script: pulls Google Search Console daily/monthly/query/page data; a URL-keyword category classifier producing weekly per-section position trends; a query-text classifier grouping ALL queries into brand/матраци/топери/дивани/ліжка/шафи buckets, each query carrying CTR, desktop/mobile/tablet device breakdown, and position history in 3 selectable granularities (week/2-week/month); a site-wide device summary; and a query/page cannibalization detector (queries where 2+ pages compete for the same ranking). Also builds a biweekly-equivalent multi-granularity position history for the top-20 pages, and a previous-28-day aggregate for period-over-period trend. Writes all of it to seo_data.json.
constraints: requires env GSC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON or local gsc_key.json (fetch_gsc.py:20-22)
SITES = [{'id':'https://matroluxe.ua/','name':'Matroluxe UA'}] — URL-prefix property, only one site configured (fetch_gsc.py:46-49)
classify_category() keyword-matches URL slugs since the site has no /catalog/ path prefix — heuristic, may misclassify some product URLs (fetch_gsc.py:32-44)
classify_query() is also a keyword heuristic (brand names + product-type words in the query text) — same caveat as classify_category()

query/page weekly history is fetched fresh from the GSC API for the requested date range each run (not accumulated locally across runs) — GSC retains ~16 months of history, so no local persistence is needed
query_categories now embeds the full list of individual queries per category (not just aggregates) so the UI can drill down from a category into its keywords
also fetches a previous-28-day aggregate (no dimensions, single row) as 'prev_period', used by home.html to compute period-over-period trend

query/page history is now sliced into 14-day (biweekly) periods instead of weekly, since the person wants period-over-period comparison arrows; total_impressions is included per query/page as a proxy for search 'frequency' — GSC has no real search-volume metric, that would need an external tool (Keyword Planner/Ahrefs/Serpstat)
query/page/device/cannibalization fetches all reuse or extend the same (date,query) or (query,*) row sets fetched once per run, not one API call per feature, to keep GSC API usage bounded

performance fix: granularity buckets are computed ONCE per run (single pass over all fetched rows per granularity), not once per query — the first version called the bucketing function inside the per-query loop, which on real data volumes (thousands of queries) meant re-scanning all rows per query and could run for hours; benchmarked fix: 9000 queries / 200k rows in ~4s
evidence: fetch_gsc.py:144-224 (fetch_query_categories(), now embeds periods[] per query)

nodes.role: SEO dashboard: per-site tabs, daily/monthly period toggle, 4 KPI cards, daily clicks bar chart, weekly category position-dynamics line chart, a clickable query-category breakdown where selecting a category opens every keyword in it as a pivot table (one column per 14-day period, position + colored ▲/▼ delta arrow vs the previous period, impressions as a frequency proxy), and a separate top-pages pivot table with the same biweekly period/arrow format. A granularity selector (Тиждень/2 тижні/Місяць) controls the period-slicing shown across the category drill-down and the pages table; the drill-down table also shows CTR and desktop/mobile position columns per query. A device-summary row (desktop/mobile/tablet clicks share, CTR, position) sits under the KPI cards, and a new cannibalization section lists queries where multiple site pages compete for the same ranking.
constraints: fails open with a visible error box if seo_data.json is missing or invalid JSON (seo.html: load()/showError())
evidence: seo.html:383-419 (selectQueryCategory(), now renders the same period pivot table)
seo.html:792-890 (renderPageHistory(), page dropped/search/sort parity with query drill-down)

nodes.role: Navigation hub / operations-center overview: dark glassmorphism theme, live system-status pills (Meta Ads, GSC), and two summary cards (SMM, SEO) with sparkline charts, linking out to index.html and seo.html. Each card also shows a period-over-period trend badge (SMM: leads, last 30d vs previous 30d computed client-side from data.json's 90-day history; SEO: clicks, last 28d vs prev_period from seo_data.json). A third glass card (CRM) mirrors SMM/SEO: live stats aggregated client-side from bitrix_data.json's raw deals/leads arrays (deals, won, lost, leads) using stage semantics from meta.stages, a purple sparkline, a period-over-period trend badge (deals count, last 30d vs prev 30d), a Bitrix24 system-status pill, and a link to bitrix.html. Card grid layout switched from a fixed 2-column grid to auto-fit (minmax 340px) to accommodate a variable number of cards.
entrypoints: loadSMM() and loadSEO() called at script end (home.html)
constraints: ONLINE/OFFLINE status pills are derived purely from whether the corresponding fetch() succeeds, not from any real health-check endpoint (home.html: setSys())

Python script: pulls Deals and Leads from Bitrix24 CRM via REST API (incoming webhook auth) and writes them as SLIM ROW-PER-RECORD data (date, stage/status, amount, manager_id, UTM fields) plus reference dictionaries (stage semantics, lead statuses/sources, user names) — mirroring how fetch_meta.py ships data.json, so bitrix.html can freely re-aggregate by any date range/dimension client-side instead of being locked to server-precomputed summaries. Also fetches overdue (incomplete, past-deadline) tasks with responsible-manager names attached.
constraints: pulls last 90 days (DAYS_BACK) of Deals/Leads by DATE_CREATE

WON-stage detection is heuristic: stage_id == 'WON' or ends with ':WON' (Bitrix's convention for non-default pipelines) — a portal with custom stage IDs not following this convention would need adjustment
pulls last 90 days (DAYS_BACK) of Deals/Leads by DATE_CREATE
won/lost deal detection uses crm.dealcategory.stage.list's SEMANTICS field (S/F/P) merged onto each deal's STAGE_ID — robust across custom pipelines, unlike matching "WON"/"LOSE" substrings

requires env BITRIX_WEBHOOK_URL (GitHub Secret) — incoming webhook only, no OAuth; overdue-tasks fetch additionally needs the webhook's "task" scope, and fails gracefully (bitrix_data.json still written with deals/leads, overdue_tasks.error set) if that scope/method is unavailable
pulls last 90 days (DAYS_BACK) of Deals/Leads by DATE_CREATE
won/lost deal detection uses crm.dealcategory.stage.list's SEMANTICS field (S/F/P), shipped in meta.stages so the frontend can classify deals the same way without re-fetching
fixed a 400 error from tasks.task.list: dropped the "!DEADLINE":"" filter and stripped microseconds from the deadline timestamp, both of which some Bitrix portals reject

nodes.role: Data artifact: raw per-deal/per-lead rows (date, stage/status, amount, manager_id, UTM fields) plus reference dictionaries (stage semantics, lead statuses/sources, user names) and overdue tasks — regenerated by fetch-bitrix and read by bitrix.html and home.html. Present in the current checkout but still in the OLDER pre-aggregated schema (deals/leads as summary objects, not arrays) — needs one more successful fetch_bitrix.py run to pick up the new raw-row schema; both bitrix.html and home.html detect the schema mismatch and show a clear message rather than silently breaking.
constraints: schema: {generated_at, period_from, deals:{total_count,total_sum,won_count,won_sum,daily[],by_stage[]}, leads:{total_count,converted_count,conversion_rate,daily[],by_status[],by_source[]}}

nodes.role: CRM dashboard: a date-range picker (Сьогодні/Вчора/7/14/30 днів/Всі + custom range, same pattern as index.html) drives client-side aggregation of the raw deals/leads arrays into KPI cards, a daily deals/leads chart, a deal funnel by stage, a per-manager stats table (deals, won, lost, leads, conversions), lead status/source breakdowns, and UTM-tagged analytics with sums. A separate (period-independent) overdue-tasks section shows bucket counts (1-3/4-7/8-14/15+ days), a per-responsible breakdown, and the oldest overdue items.
constraints: fails open with a visible error box if bitrix_data.json is missing or invalid JSON (bitrix.html: load()/showError())
evidence: bitrix.html:322-380 (aggregateDeals()/aggregateLeads(), client-side re-aggregation for any date range)
